examples/demo-app/access.mjs.title: An admin can export only their own workspace's reports
examples/demo-app/access.mjs.oldLogic: Any user whose role is admin passes the export check. The target workspace is not checked, so an admin from another workspace also passes.
examples/demo-app/access.mjs.newLogic: The user must be an admin and their workspace ID must equal the target workspace ID. An admin from another workspace is rejected.
examples/demo-app/access.mjs.whatChanged: Export permission now depends on workspace membership as well as role. The exportPage caller uses this helper before returning rows.
examples/demo-app/access.mjs.whyHumanReview: Should support staff or organization-wide admins be able to export across workspaces? Confirm the intended permission boundary and where both workspace IDs come from.

examples/demo-app/pagination.mjs.title: Page sizes are normalized and capped at 100 rows
examples/demo-app/pagination.mjs.oldLogic: The requested value is converted to a number, with falsy results falling back to 20. Negative, fractional, infinite, and very large numbers are otherwise returned.
examples/demo-app/pagination.mjs.newLogic: Non-finite numbers and values below 1 fall back to 20. Positive values are rounded down to an integer, then capped at 100.
examples/demo-app/pagination.mjs.whatChanged: The export caller receives a bounded positive integer. Requests above 100 no longer produce equally large export pages.
examples/demo-app/pagination.mjs.whyHumanReview: Is 100 the intended export limit, and should invalid sizes fall back to 20 rather than return an error? Confirm those product choices.

examples/demo-app/greeting.mjs.title: Greeting uses template-string syntax
examples/demo-app/greeting.mjs.oldLogic: The greeting joins a literal prefix, the supplied name, and an exclamation mark with string concatenation.
examples/demo-app/greeting.mjs.newLogic: The greeting interpolates the supplied name inside a template string with the same prefix and punctuation.
examples/demo-app/greeting.mjs.whatChanged: The syntax is shorter and produces the same text for ordinary string names. JavaScript object coercion can differ between concatenation and interpolation, so this is not a universal equivalence for every possible input.
examples/demo-app/greeting.mjs.whyHumanReview: If callers can pass objects with custom coercion instead of strings, check that edge case. For the intended string-name use, this is a small syntax cleanup.

examples/demo-app/README.md.title: Fix a spelling mistake in the demo documentation
examples/demo-app/README.md.oldLogic: The description of the greeting helper spells message as mesage.
examples/demo-app/README.md.whatChanged: One word in a Markdown document is corrected. No executable code changes in this hunk.
examples/demo-app/README.md.whyHumanReview: No product decision is apparent in this spelling correction. The original diff is available if you want to verify it.
